title.narrative: Helping Enterprises Access Liquidity in the Republic of Croatia

description.narrative: The development objectives of Helping Enterprises Access Liquidity Project for Croatia are: (i) to support the recovery of private sector exporters from the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic; (ii) enhance access to finance for firms in underserved segments and lagging regions; and (iii) to strengthen HBOR's institutional capacity as a development bank. The project has a single component to reflect the use of project proceeds, but forty percent of the funds are conditional on the achievements of performance-based conditions (PBCs) in support of Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR's) institutional capacity strengthening. The use of all loan proceeds is the same - to provide sub-loans to eligible project beneficiaries.

The project development objectives are: (i) to support the recovery of private sector exporters from the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, (ii) enhance access to finance for firms in underserved segments and lagging regions, and (iii) to strengthen HBOR's institutional capacity as a development bank.

title.narrative: Increased use of EU funds by HBOR

comment.narrative:
The indicator was calculated as a ratio of EU funding (disbursed) as percent of total sources of funding of HBOR. The amount of EU funds refers to the overall amount where HBOR is the implementing body of both EU funds allocated from the national level and special financial arrangements with EC (i.e., centrally managed EU funds). The total sources of funding were calculated as a sum o: (i) borrowings and debt securities issued, (ii) capital contributed from the budget of the Republic of Croatia, and (iii) EU funding.
The target (8.00) has been achieved with the final result of 8.63%.

Compliance with prudential regulations monitors financial performance of PFIs. By decision of the HBOR Management Board no.: 1100-55-45/2024 of December 5, 2024, the report of the Financial Institutions Analysis and Economic Research Directorate "Annual assessment of banks 2023" was taken into account, and the new internal ratings of banks are applied from the date of adoption of the decision. One bank has not been compliant with prudential regulations according to the report. This PFI (Imex banka d.d.) is not included in the implementation of the HEAL Project. The assessment of banks for 2024 is under way. It will be submitted to the HBOR decision-making bodies at the end of September 2025, in line with new Methodology for assigning ratings to banks (May 2025). A change in the levels of internal ratings will be seen according to preliminary calculation, but no disruptions in the operations of banks have been observed that indicate a deterioration in their risk profile.

Target achieved (100%). By decision of the HBOR Management Board no.: 1100-40-30/2025 of October 9, 2025, the report of the Financial Institutions Analysis and Economic Research Directorate "Annual assessment of banks 2024" was taken into account, and the new internal ratings of banks are applied from the date of adoption of the decision. Banks that participated in co-financing in 2024 have been compliant with prudential regulations according to the report.

title.narrative: Number of exporters receiving sub-loans under the project that remain solvent

comment.narrative:
This indicator measured the continued viability i.e. recovery of private exporters from the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic by using the Financial Agency's (FINA) data by monitoring if a project-supported exporter was put under enforcement due to unsettled obligations. The FINA records all business entities transactions, time deposits and other financial data, and conducts the enforcement of the monetary funds.
The target (90%) of exporters receiving sub-loans under the project that remain solvent has been achieved (100% of exporters receiving sub-loans remained solvent).
